A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method to study cavities of proteins by NMR, which is based on the use of SF6 as a reporter.
SF(6) can be used as a spy molecule for detecting cavities in proteins and the (19) F NMR signal is a sensitive probe to study the binding of SF6 to the cavities.
SF(6) can be used to detect the presence of cavities in proteins, and the cavity size can be estimated from the (19)SF chemical shift, line shape, and longitudinal relaxation time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the (19)H{(19)}F heteronuclear Overhouser effect is a useful tool for detecting the binding of SF6 in a hydrophobic cavity of proteins.

(1)H{19)F} NMR experiments can be used to probe hydrophobic cavieties in proteins by detecting the binding of a small molecule, such as SF(6), which can be detected by its own (19)F resonance and by intermolecular (19)F{1H} HOEs.
the (19) F chemical shift and the HOE are two complementary NMR parameters for the detection of SF(6).
